subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: The Olmsted Legacy
description: A 60-second lesson on The Olmsted Legacy.

hook.text: Frederick Law Olmsted designed Central Park, Prospect Park, and the Emerald Necklace. He invented landscape architecture.

buildup.text: Olmsted believed parks healed the stress of urban life. He called them the 'lungs of the city.'

discovery.text: He separated pedestrians, carriages, and cross-traffic using sunken roads — a traffic innovation still used today.

twist.text: Olmsted was hospitalized for mental illness late in life. The parks he designed for healing couldn't heal him.

climax.text: His firm designed over 500 parks, campuses, and estates. The profession he created now shapes every city.

punchline.text: He gave cities their lungs. The profession he invented still breathes.

quiz.question: What traffic innovation did Olmsted pioneer in Central Park?
options: One-way carriage lanes to reduce congestion
Sunken roads separating pedestrians from cross-traffic
Dedicated horse-riding trails alongside walking paths
